plan.plan: WORKLOAD DERIVATION (Little's Law, not server cap): 4 extraction targets (14 CFR 65.91 eligibility, 65.93 privileges/limitations, 1.1/43 Appendix A 'major alteration' definition cross-reference, 65.95/65.97 continuity/renewal conditions) = 4 units. Throughput = 1 Compliance Specialist × 1 unit per 45 min = 1.33 units/hr. Duration = 4 / 1.33 = 3.0 hours (canonical figure; budget = 3.0 hr, 1 worker, 0 remainder; no cap baked in). Cost = $0 (public eCFR, no licenses/components). STEP 1 — Source lock: Access https://www.ecfr.gov/; confirm current 14 CFR. Kill trigger: if eCFR unavailable or version non-current, stop until resolved. STEP 2 — Triage: Navigate to Part 65 Subpart D (Inspection Authorization). Confirm sections 65.91, 65.93, 65.95, 65.97 exist. Cross-reference 14 CFR 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A for 'major alteration' definition. Kill trigger: if Subpart D lacks these sections, abort and re-identify correct part/subpart; do not derive on missing topology. STEP 3 — Extract qualification text: Capture verbatim requirements for initial IA certification (65.91 prerequisites: 2 years A&P, passed IA exam, etc.) and IA privileges (65.93 authority to approve major alterations/major repairs when performed per approved data). Note that major-alteration approval under IA is tied to privilege language and approved technical data, not just certification eligibility. STEP 4 — Definition integration: Quote current 14 CFR 1.1 'major alteration' definition and Part 43 Appendix A criteria; link explicitly to 65.93 privilege context so AMT sees when alteration approval applies versus inspection-only. STEP 5 — Structure: Deliver table (Section | Topic | Key Qualification/Privilege | Direct URL | Note) plus bullet summary for AMT/regulator audience. Each of the 4 targets must carry a live eCFR URL (e.g., https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91). STEP 6 — Validation: Compliance Specialist performs second read of all 4 cited sections against live source; verify URLs resolve and text is current. FALSIFIER (disprovable): Completeness metric — if < 4 cited sections with live URLs are verified within the 4-hour session window, sizing is wrong; respond by increasing concurrency to 2 specialists and extending duration to 6.0 hours (4 targets / (2 × 1.33) = 1.5 hr + 4.5 hr verification overhead = 6.0 hr).

The document explicitly separates initial IA certification qualifications (65.91 prerequisites) from ongoing IA privileges regarding major alterations (65.93), with no ambiguous blended statements.
The regulatory definition of 'major alteration' is quoted or precisely referenced from the current eCFR and explicitly tied to the IA privilege context under 65.93.

The output is formatted as a structured table or bullet reference readable by a certificated FAA-AMT or regulator without requiring external explanation.

All procedural assumptions (Part 65 Subpart D as primary source, current eCFR version) are documented with kill triggers; none alter the 4-section scope unless a trigger fires, and the falsifier metric (<4 verified sections in 4-hour window) is recorded.

# INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) QUALIFICATIONS FOR MAJOR ALTERATIONS
## FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician (AMT) Reference Document

---

### SOURCE LOCK STATUS
**Primary Source:** Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR)
**Base URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/
**Title:** 14 CFR (Aeronautics and Space)
**Target Part:** Part 65, Subpart D — Inspection Authorization

**Kill Trigger Status:** 
- eCFR availability: Cannot verify (no live access)
- Version currency: Cannot verify (no live access)
- Subpart D section existence: Cannot verify (no live access)

**LIMITATION NOTICE:** This document was prepared without live access to eCFR. URLs follow standard eCFR patterns but resolution and currency cannot be verified. A Compliance Specialist with live access must perform STEP 6 validation before operational use.

---

### SECTION 1: INITIAL IA CERTIFICATION ELIGIBILITY (14 CFR § 65.91)

**Direct URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/section-65.91

**Topic:** Eligibility Prerequisites for Inspection Authorization

| Requirement | Regulatory Basis | Notes |
|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| Hold mechanic certificate | § 65.91(a) | Must hold current mechanic certificate with BOTH airframe AND powerplant ratings |
| Certificate duration | § 65.91(a)(1) | Must have held A&P ratings for at least 3 years prior to IA application |
| Active maintenance experience | § 65.91(a)(2) | Must have been engaged in maintenance work for at least 2 of the 5 years preceding application |
| Fixed base of operations | § 65.91(a)(3) | Must have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during normal business hours |
| Equipment access | § 65.91(a)(4) | Must have access to equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to perform IA functions |
| Written examination | § 65.91(b) | Must pass a written test on inspection standards applicable to major repairs and major alterations |

**Key Distinction:** Section 65.91 establishes WHO may obtain IA certification. It does NOT define what an IA may do once certified—that authority comes from § 65.93.

---

### SECTION 2: IA PRIVILEGES AND LIMITATIONS (14 CFR § 65.93)

**Direct URL:** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/section-65.93

**Topic:** Privileges — Authority to Approve Major Alterations

| Privilege | Regulatory Basis | Conditions/Limitations |
|-----------|-------------------|------------------------|
| Inspect and approve major repairs | § 65.93(a)(1) | Work must be performed in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator |
| Inspect and approve major alterations | § 65.93(a)(1) | Work must be performed in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator |
| Perform annual inspections | § 65.93(a)(2) | On aircraft of 12,500 lbs or less maximum certificated takeoff weight |
| Perform progressive inspections | § 65.93(a)(3) | As authorized by the Administrator |

**Critical Privilege Boundary:** An IA holder's authority to approve major alterations is NOT automatic. The privilege under § 65.93(a)(1) is CONDITIONAL upon:
1. The work being performed in accordance with Administrator-approved technical data; AND
2. The alteration meeting the regulatory definition of "major alteration" per 14 CFR § 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A

**Limitation:** An IA may NOT approve alterations that require approval under a type certificate or STC process outside the scope of approved data.

---

### SECTION 3: MAJOR ALTERATION DEFINITION (14 CFR § 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A)

**Definition Source URLs:**
- § 1.1 Definitions: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-1.1
- Part 43 Appendix A: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-43/appendix-A

**Regulatory Definition (14 CFR § 1.1):**

> "Major alteration" means an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that:
> 
> (1) Might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or
> 
> (2) Is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.

**Part 43 Appendix A — Major Alteration Categories:**

| Category | Examples of Major Alterations |
|----------|-------------------------------|
| Airframe | Changes to wings, control surfaces, fuselage structure, landing gear, hydraulic/electrical systems affecting airworthiness |
| Powerplant | Changes to engine, fuel system, exhaust, cooling system, propeller not listed in specifications |
| Propeller | Changes to blade design, hub, governor, or control system |
| Appliance | Alterations to instruments, radios, safety equipment affecting airworthiness |

**Integration with IA Privilege:**

The IA's authority under § 65.93 to approve major alterations is explicitly tied to this definition. An IA may approve return-to-service ONLY when:
1. The alteration meets the § 1.1/Appendix A definition of "major alteration"; AND
2. Approved technical data exists for the specific alteration; AND
3. The work was performed in accordance with that approved data

**If the alteration does NOT meet the major alteration definition:** The work is a "minor alteration" and may be approved by any appropriately rated mechanic without IA involvement.

---

### SECTION 4: IA CONTINUITY AND RENEWAL (14 CFR §§ 65.95 and 65.97)

**Direct URLs:**
- § 65.95: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/section-65.95
- § 65.97: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-65/section-65.97

**Topic:** Maintaining IA Privileges

| Requirement | Section | Details |
|-------------|---------|---------|
| Duration of authorization | § 65.95 | IA is valid for 2 years (March 31 of even-numbered years) unless surrendered, suspended, or revoked |
| Renewal requirements | § 65.95(c) | Must meet activity requirements before renewal deadline |
| Recent activity requirement | § 65.97(a) | Must have performed IA duties (inspections, approvals, instruction) or completed acceptable training |
| Activity alternatives | § 65.97(b) | Options include: (1) 8+ IA-related activities; (2) 16+ hours FAA-approved training; (3) combination thereof |
| Failure to meet requirements | § 65.97(c) | Must retake and pass the IA written examination to reinstate |

**Key Point:** IA privileges are NOT permanent. Failure to maintain recent activity under § 65.97 results in loss of IA authority, regardless of initial qualification under § 65.91.

---

### SUMMARY FOR AMT/REGULATOR AUDIENCE

**Initial IA Certification (§ 65.91):**
- Hold A&P certificate for 3+ years
- 2 years active maintenance experience in preceding 5 years
- Fixed base of operations
- Access to equipment, facilities, and data
- Pass written examination on major repair/alteration inspection standards

**IA Privileges for Major Alterations (§ 65.93):**
- Authority to inspect and approve return-to-service after major repairs AND major alterations
- CONDITION: Work must be performed per Administrator-approved technical data
- Does NOT authorize design approval—only return-to-service approval

**Major Alteration Definition (§ 1.1 + Part 43 Appendix A):**
- Alteration not in specifications that appreciably affects weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities
- OR alteration not done per accepted practices/elementary operations
- Appendix A provides categorical examples

**Maintaining IA Authority (§§ 65.95, 65.97):**
- 2-year authorization period
- Must demonstrate recent IA activity or training for renewal
- Failure to meet activity requirements requires re-examination

---
